texts.preamble: Neelesh Chaubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2026 Author: Hirdesh Bench: Hirdesh Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:11289 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Hirdesh On The 7 th Of April, 2026 Misc. Petition No. 1936 of 2026 Neelesh Chaubey Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance: Shri Sanjay Kumar Bahirani - Advocate for the petitioner Shri Dileep Awasthi - Government Advocate for State. Order
texts.facts: 2. Brief facts of the case are that the Food Safety Officer inspected the petitioner's firm, where the petitioner was found present and operating the business. During inspection, various food articles such as mixed milk, skimmed curd, ghee, and paneer, which were being used for preparation and sale for human consumption at the premises, were found stored in the shop. On inspection, the said articles were found to be sub-standard and misbranded. Accordingly, samples were taken and sent for analysis to the Public Analyst, Bhopal, who submitted a report wherein some of the samples were found to be misbranded. 3. Thereafter, the Food Safety Officer filed a private complaint before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11289 2 MP-1936-2026 Adjudicating Officer, who issued a show-cause notice to the petitioner. The petitioner filed his reply denying the allegations. 4. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 28.11.2024, the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal along with an application for condonation of delay under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
texts.arguments: 5. Aggrieved by the impugned order of the Appellate Tribunal, the petitioner has filed the present petition contending that the impugned order is not in consonance with the spirit of law and that the appeal ought not to have been dismissed solely on the ground of limitation. It is submitted that sufficient cause was shown for condonation of delay by stating that the copy of the impugned order dated 28.11.2024 was received on 05.12.2024, and thereafter the petitioner contacted his counsel, and the appeal was filed on 28.01.2025. Thus, the delay of near about 25 days is bona fide and inadvertent. Hence, prayer has been made for setting aside the impugned order. 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State supported the impugned order and prayed for dismissal of the petition. According to Rule 3.3.1 Food Safety and Standards Act:- Every appeal under Section 70 of the Act arising out of a decision of the Adjudicating Officer appointed under Section 68 of the Act, shall be filed within a period of 30 days from the date on which the copy of the order against which the appeal is filed, is received by the appellant. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11289 3 MP-1936-2026 Provided, however, that the Appellate Tribunal may allow a maximum of another 30 days to entertain an appeal if it is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing the appeal within first 30 days. 9. 11. The Apex Court in the case of N.Balakrishnan Vs. M. Krishnamurthy (1998) 7 SCC 123 in Para 10 and 11 has held as under:- 10. Rules of limitation are not meant to destroy the rights of parties.
